original_value: The effective fault diagnosis in the prognostic and health management of reciprocating compressors has been a research hotspot for a long time. The vibration signal of reciprocating compressors is nonlinear and non-stationary. However, the traditional methods applied to processing such signals have three issues, including separating the useful frequency bands from overlapped signals, extracting fault features with strong subjectivity, and processing the massive data with limited learning abilities. To address the above issues, this paper, which is based on the idea of deep learning, proposed an intelligent fault diagnosis method combining Local Mean Decomposition (LMD) and the Stack Denoising Autoencoder (SDAE). The vibration signal is firstly decomposed by LMD and reconstructed based on the cross-correlation criterion. The virtual noise channel is constructed to reduce the noise of the vibration signal. Then, the de-noised signal is input into the trained SDAE model to learn the fault features adaptively. Finally, the conditions of the reciprocating compressor valve are classified by the proposed method. The results show that classification accuracy is 92.72% under the condition of a low signal-noise ratio, which is 5 percentage points higher than that of the traditional methods. This shows the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

result.paraphrase: Effective fault diagnosis in prognostic and health management for reciprocating compressors has long been a research focus. Their vibration signals are nonlinear and non-stationary, while conventional signal-processing methods face three main problems: difficulty isolating useful frequency bands from overlapping signals, highly subjective fault-feature extraction, and limited ability to handle large-scale data. To overcome these issues, this paper proposes an intelligent fault diagnosis approach based on deep learning that combines Local Mean Decomposition (LMD) with a Stack Denoising Autoencoder (SDAE). First, the vibration signal is decomposed by LMD and reconstructed using the cross-correlation criterion. A virtual noise channel is then built to reduce signal noise. Next, the denoised signal is fed into the trained SDAE model for adaptive fault-feature learning. Finally, the reciprocating compressor valve condition is classified by the proposed method. The results indicate a classification accuracy of 92.72% under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions, 5 percentage points higher than traditional methods, demonstrating the method’s effectiveness and robustness.
